listing.name: Rocket: Robot on Wheels (Rocket-R)
listing.summary: Play Rocket: Robot on Wheels with your own matching US game file.

steps.title: Select your own Rocket ROM on first Play
steps.instruction: On first Play, choose your own supported Rocket: Robot on Wheels US ROM in the upstream launcher. It verifies the game and remembers the chosen path. Use the upstream menus for controls and compatible mods; no game compilation or separate installer is needed for the published player.

steps.title: Keep saves and mod profiles separately backed up
steps.instruction: Default Windows saves, settings, mod profiles, mod-specific saves, logs and crash reports use %APPDATA%/Rocket-R. Keep a separate backup of the actual profile before changing versions; older versions may not read newer saves. Its external profile is outside Portcove backup and runtime rollback; rollback does not rewind saves. Keep each release’s own bundled engine/mod resources together, and keep custom --config or developer paths backed up separately.

steps.title: Choose the Linux package for your system
steps.instruction: On x64 or ARM64 Linux, make the matching AppImage executable and open it. The packaged game needs glibc 2.35 and GLIBCXX 3.4.30. If you use a Portable archive, unpack the whole folder and run Launch-Rocket-R.sh. On Steam Deck, unpack the separate x64 Steam Deck archive and run START-ROCKET-R.sh from its folder. It launches the included AppDir directly.

steps.title: Open Rocket-R on Android
steps.instruction: Install the ARM64 APK on Android 7 or later on a device with the required Vulkan 1.2 features. Open Rocket-R and choose your matching US ROM. The app keeps a private ROM copy and its saves and settings. Back up what you can access before clearing app storage or uninstalling. The upstream Android build is experimental, and some devices may fail to start it.

references.title: Check your original game file
references.instruction: Rocket-R accepts your own US game with code NSUE, 12 MiB and canonical SHA-1 622d71a44da0b81ea68092cac9198c66154a4f4a. The desktop launcher accepts .z64, .n64 and .v64 files.

references.title: Find your Linux profile and launch logs
references.instruction: By default the game uses $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rocket-r or ~/.config/rocket-r for settings, saves and mod profiles. A custom --config path or the rocket-r-data fallback changes where you need to back up. The upstream launcher records logs in $XDG_STATE_HOME/rocket-r or ~/.local/state/rocket-r, with a temporary-directory fallback when needed.

presentation.manual_preparation: On first Play, choose your own supported Rocket: Robot on Wheels US ROM in the upstream launcher. It verifies the game and remembers the chosen path. Use the upstream menus for controls and compatible mods; no game compilation or separate installer is needed for the published player. Default Windows saves, settings, mod profiles, mod-specific saves, logs and crash reports use %APPDATA%/Rocket-R. Keep a separate backup of the actual profile before changing versions; older versions may not read newer saves. Portcove preserves only the declared rocket-r-data in-folder fallback for its managed Windows copy. Its external profile is outside Portcove backup and runtime rollback; rollback does not rewind saves. Keep each release’s own bundled engine/mod resources together, and keep custom --config or developer paths backed up separately. Existing external copies retain their files and runtime update owner.
